paragraphs.source_en: Murad I is memorialised in much later Ottoman chronicles as a gazi warrior and miracle-working saint. In European histories, he is remembered for having been cut down in battle on the Field of Blackbirds in Kosovo in 1389. Despite the fact that the Serbs lost their King Lazar and the Ottomans won the battle, the event is commemorated to this day in Serbia. The Ottoman victory led to nearly five hundred years of Ottoman rule over the Serbs. But even with these conquests, Murad I made a more significant mark on Ottoman history by instituting policies that contributed to the Ottoman dynasty’s long-term staying power and success. He changed titular customs, elite recruitment, and succession practices. Murad I organised the first Janissary (yeni ¢eri, literally, ‘new army’ or ‘new soldiers’) units from prisoners of war taken in battle in Christian-ruled regions.
